groups.title: BC Liberal → BC United
groups.intro: The recovered set follows the Liberal identity from a 1996 campaign badge through map, sun and provincial-landscape designs to the 2023 BC United brand. The registered-name date and public brand launch are recorded separately. The 2024 withdrawal from the election is a campaign event; this catalogue does not call it a merger with the Conservatives.

groups.title: B.C. Conservatives
groups.intro: Historical mountain motifs, script wordmarks, the 2020 Conservative British Columbia treatment and the 2022 C-and-landscape identity are represented. Earlier logo date ranges rely on secondary attribution; recent designs are corroborated by official party documents.

groups.title: CCF → BC NDP
groups.intro: A 1949 CCF campaign specimen precedes a 1983 NDP riding campaign lockup and generic NDP arrangements documented in 1996, 2005 and 2017. The modern italic sun-box form appears in a dated April 2017 advertisement, before the “2023” filenames of the current downloads. The upright third-party vector’s upload date does not establish a later party redesign.

groups.title: Social Credit
groups.intro: Primary documents and newspaper advertisements provide a 1937 name specimen, a 1950 circle-and-cross emblem, a 1969 voting signature, BC-profile layouts in 1979 and 1983, and a 1986 campaign wordmark. These are dated observations, not a complete succession of exclusive logo eras. “League” and “Party” wording is preserved as it appears in the sources.

groups.title: BC Greens
groups.intro: The collection contains the sunflower design, the “Greens of British Columbia” wordmark, current “BC greens” artwork, and Emily Lowan leader-name treatments. Colours and file formats are grouped together. A leader’s name on a lockup is not a legal party renaming.

groups.title: Reform BC and Democratic Reform
groups.intro: Two separately identified parties are shown here. Reform BC’s flag-and-sun logo is a provincial identity. Democratic Reform B.C.’s earlier registered names were B.C. Democratic Alliance and British Columbia Democratic Coalition; the official name-change chain is separate from the Progressive Democratic Alliance.

groups.title: OneBC
groups.intro: The official website and a candidate media kit supply gold/navy and gold/white treatments, with a small icon and a Commons vector copy. The recovered material documents one wordmark family. No separate historical redesign is established.

groups.title: CentreBC
groups.intro: A 2025 stacked blue-wave copy differs from the horizontal red-wave treatment retrieved from the official website in 2026. A 2026 campaign response also uses a white-on-red badge. These differences are visible in the sources, while exact adoption dates and replacement relationships remain unverified.

groups.title: Provincial Party — 1923–1924 specimens
groups.intro: Two small name specimens come from photographs of an original platform and letterhead. They document the printed party name, rather than establish a standardized graphic emblem. Both are retained at their recovered resolution.
